Compute the mean squared error between predicted and analytical distances [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the mean squared error is computed between predicted and analytical distances. Both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly define a loss function (often referred to as sphere loss) that calculates the squared difference between the predicted signed distance function (SDF) values and the analytical SDF values for a sphere (defined as the L2 norm of the point coordinates minus the radius), and then averages this value (mean). This matches the definition of Mean Squared Error (MSE).
